summary: A trim stops deleting when the WAL passes 256 MiB and restarts it, so the WAL stays bounded while a cut runs on a busy member

schema.detail: No table or claim schema change.

rules.detail: The same claims are deleted in the same chunks. The rules version and digest are unchanged.

compatibility.detail: Local to each member, with no wire or stored format change. A trim writes nearly all the time, and a busy daemon nearly always has a reader on an older snapshot, so the idle recycle never found the WAL fully copied and the WAL grew for as long as the trim ran. Now, once the WAL passes 65,536 frames, the trim stops deleting and restarts the WAL: it copies the pages off the writer until every frame is, flushes them, then, at the writer's turn, waits up to 200 ms for readers begun in between and runs a RESTART checkpoint, so the next write starts the WAL from its beginning. An attempt that cannot copy every frame leaves the writer alone. Under a daemon on a 57 GB store copy, a restart held the writer at most 187 ms. If the WAL will not restart within 30 s, the run stops where it is, the cut stays trimming, and the next checkpoint step goes on. Each wait is logged. Shared and local trims both get it.

manual.detail: No manual step. A member paused with [trim] daily_claims = 1 can return to its usual cap once it runs this release.

recovery.detail: Revert the build. A running trim keeps its cursor and goes on.
